questions.prompt: Which nutrient is mainly required for growth, repair and maintenance of body tissues?
options: Protein
Vitamin C
Water
Dietary fibre
questions.correctAnswer: Protein
questions.explanation: Protein supplies amino acids used to build and repair body tissues during growth and recovery.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify major nutrients and relate them to body functions.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is needed in haemoglobin for transport of oxygen in the blood?
options: Iron
Iodine
Calcium
Sodium
questions.correctAnswer: Iron
questions.explanation: Iron forms part of haemoglobin, the pigment that carries oxygen in red blood cells.
questions.learningOutcome: State functions of selected mineral elements in human nutrition.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is most closely linked to blood clotting?
options: Vitamin K
Vitamin A
Vitamin B1
Vitamin D
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin K
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is needed for the formation of clotting factors that help stop bleeding.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise key functions of fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of blanching vegetables before freezing?
options: To slow enzyme action before storage
To make freezing unnecessary
To remove all nutrients
To ferment the vegetables
questions.correctAnswer: To slow enzyme action before storage
questions.explanation: Brief heating slows enzymes that can spoil colour, flavour and texture during frozen storage.
questions.learningOutcome: State reasons for common pre-treatment steps in food preservation.

questions.prompt: Which condition is most important for growth of many food-spoilage microorganisms?
options: Moisture
Complete dryness
Sterile packaging
Freezing temperature
questions.correctAnswer: Moisture
questions.explanation: Microorganisms usually need available water to grow, so drying helps slow spoilage.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify conditions that encourage or reduce food spoilage.

questions.prompt: Which kitchen practice directly reduces cross-contamination between raw chicken and cooked food?
options: Use separate clean boards and utensils
Store both foods uncovered together
Taste with the same spoon repeatedly
Wipe hands on a dirty cloth
questions.correctAnswer: Use separate clean boards and utensils
questions.explanation: Separate clean equipment prevents microorganisms on raw food from reaching ready-to-eat food.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify hygiene practices that prevent contamination during food preparation.

questions.prompt: Which textile fibre is obtained from sheep fleece?
options: Wool
Cotton
Linen
Nylon
questions.correctAnswer: Wool
questions.explanation: Wool is an animal fibre commonly obtained from sheep fleece.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources of common natural and manufactured fibres.

questions.prompt: In garment construction, what is the main purpose of a dart?
options: To shape fabric to fit body contours
To remove stains from cloth
To test food freshness
To measure household income
questions.correctAnswer: To shape fabric to fit body contours
questions.explanation: A dart removes fullness from fabric so a garment fits curved parts of the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Define garment construction terms and their purposes.

questions.prompt: Which laundry document symbol usually means a garment should not be bleached?
options: A triangle crossed out
A plain circle
A square with one line
A hand inside a basin
questions.correctAnswer: A triangle crossed out
questions.explanation: Care labels commonly use a crossed-out triangle to warn against bleaching.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret common laundry care symbols used on garments.

questions.prompt: Which consumer document is issued to show payment for goods or services?
options: Receipt
Recipe card
Pattern piece
Duty roster
questions.correctAnswer: Receipt
questions.explanation: A receipt records payment details and can support returns, complaints or budgeting records.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify documents used in consumer transactions.

questions.prompt: Which organisation mark on goods in Kenya helps show that a product meets approved standards?
options: KEBS standardization mark
School timetable mark
Recipe testing mark
Home duty mark
questions.correctAnswer: KEBS standardization mark
questions.explanation: The Kenya Bureau of Standards mark helps consumers identify products that meet relevant standards.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise consumer information used to judge product quality and safety.

questions.prompt: Which household resource is classified as a human resource?
options: Skill
Money
Land
Equipment
questions.correctAnswer: Skill
questions.explanation: Skill belongs to people and affects how well tasks are planned and carried out.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify human and non-human resources used in home management.

questions.prompt: Which colour-scheme term refers to using one colour with its tints and shades?
options: Monochromatic
Complementary
Triadic
Neutral-only
questions.correctAnswer: Monochromatic
questions.explanation: A monochromatic scheme is based on one hue varied through lighter and darker values.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify design vocabulary used in interior planning.

questions.prompt: Which safety item is most suitable for covering a small clean wound after washing hands?
options: Sterile dressing
Tailor's chalk
Detergent powder
Measuring tape
questions.correctAnswer: Sterile dressing
questions.explanation: A sterile dressing protects a clean wound from dirt and reduces infection risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify first-aid materials used for common minor injuries.

questions.prompt: Which family record helps track expected income, planned spending and savings?
options: Household budget
Care label
Pattern envelope
Recipe method
questions.correctAnswer: Household budget
questions.explanation: A household budget compares available income with planned expenses and savings goals.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify records used to manage family resources.

questions.prompt: Why should vitamin C rich foods be included with plant sources of iron such as beans or sukuma wiki?
options: Vitamin C improves absorption of non-haem iron
Vitamin C turns iron into calcium
Vitamin C removes all fibre from the meal
Vitamin C makes protein unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Vitamin C improves absorption of non-haem iron
questions.explanation: Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron from plant foods more effectively.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how nutrient combinations affect absorption and health.

questions.prompt: Which meal best balances energy, protein, protective foods and water for a senior school learner?
options: Githeri with vegetables, avocado and clean water
Plain tea with sugar only
Soda and crisps only
Chapati without any accompaniment
questions.correctAnswer: Githeri with vegetables, avocado and clean water
questions.explanation: The meal combines carbohydrate, plant protein, vegetables, healthy fat and fluid.
questions.learningOutcome: Select balanced meals using locally available foods.

questions.prompt: Why should an adolescent who is very physically active eat enough complex carbohydrates?
options: They provide sustained energy for activity
They replace the need for sleep
They prevent all injuries
They change into vitamins immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They provide sustained energy for activity
questions.explanation: Complex carbohydrates from cereals, roots and tubers supply energy needed for school and physical activity.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain nutrition needs for adolescents with different activity levels.

questions.prompt: Which cooking practice best conserves water-soluble vitamins in green vegetables?
options: Cook briefly in little water and serve soon
Boil for a long time in plenty of water
Cut and leave uncovered for many hours
Add baking soda and keep reheating
questions.correctAnswer: Cook briefly in little water and serve soon
questions.explanation: Short cooking with limited water reduces loss of heat-sensitive and water-soluble vitamins.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply cooking practices that reduce nutrient loss.

questions.prompt: Why is standardisation important when preparing a recipe for sale in a school snack project?
options: It gives consistent quality, portion size and costing
It makes hygiene unnecessary
It removes the need for packaging
It allows random ingredient changes each day
questions.correctAnswer: It gives consistent quality, portion size and costing
questions.explanation: A standard recipe helps the producer control quality, yield and cost each time the product is made.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of standard recipes in food production.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to thicken a sauce with starch. Why should starch be mixed with cold liquid before adding it to hot liquid?
options: To separate starch grains and reduce lump formation
To make the sauce taste raw
To stop gelatinisation completely
To remove all flavour from the sauce
questions.correctAnswer: To separate starch grains and reduce lump formation
questions.explanation: Cold mixing disperses starch so it can gelatinise more evenly when heated.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain practical principles used in preparing starch-based dishes.

questions.prompt: Why should milk be kept cold during storage and transport?
options: Low temperature slows bacterial multiplication
Cold storage turns milk into a dry food
Cold storage removes all lactose
Low temperature makes dirty containers safe
questions.correctAnswer: Low temperature slows bacterial multiplication
questions.explanation: Milk is perishable, and refrigeration slows the growth of microorganisms that cause spoilage and illness.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe storage practices for perishable foods.

questions.prompt: Which sign most clearly suggests that cooking oil has become rancid?
options: Unpleasant stale smell and off flavour
Clear golden colour only
Sealed new container
Normal expiry date in the future
questions.correctAnswer: Unpleasant stale smell and off flavour
questions.explanation: Rancidity produces stale odours and off flavours as fats oxidise or break down.
questions.learningOutcome: Use quality indicators when selecting and storing food items.

questions.prompt: Why is fermentation useful in preparing some foods such as yoghurt or sour porridge?
options: Useful microorganisms produce desirable flavour and acidity
It always makes food sterile without heat
It changes all nutrients into water
It removes the need for clean equipment
questions.correctAnswer: Useful microorganisms produce desirable flavour and acidity
questions.explanation: Controlled fermentation can improve flavour and preservation, but it still requires hygiene.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of microorganisms in controlled food fermentation.

questions.prompt: Which fabric property makes polyester suitable for some sportswear?
options: It dries quickly and resists creasing
It always absorbs more moisture than cotton
It is destroyed by all washing
It cannot be blended with other fibres
questions.correctAnswer: It dries quickly and resists creasing
questions.explanation: Polyester is a manufactured fibre that dries fast and resists wrinkles, although comfort depends on fabric construction.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate fibre properties to suitable clothing uses.

questions.prompt: Why is grain line important when laying a pattern on woven fabric?
options: It helps the garment hang and keep its intended shape
It makes fabric colour permanent
It removes the need for seam allowances
It changes woven fabric into knitted fabric
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the garment hang and keep its intended shape
questions.explanation: Correct grain placement supports fit, balance and stability in the finished garment.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain principles of accurate pattern layout before cutting.

questions.prompt: A machine seam has loops on the underside of the fabric. Which adjustment should be checked first?
options: Threading and upper tension
Room ventilation
Food label date
Furniture arrangement
questions.correctAnswer: Threading and upper tension
questions.explanation: Looping commonly results from incorrect threading or unsuitable tension settings on the sewing machine.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common causes of machine stitching faults.

questions.prompt: Why should coloured garments be sorted before laundering?
options: To prevent dye transfer and choose suitable washing methods
To make all clothes shrink equally
To avoid rinsing completely
To increase detergent residue
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent dye transfer and choose suitable washing methods
questions.explanation: Sorting by colour, fabric type and soil level protects garments and improves cleaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for sorting garments before washing.

questions.prompt: Which first step is safest before using a stain remover on a coloured fabric?
options: Test it on an inconspicuous area
Iron the stain to fix it
Mix all removers together
Scrub with sand immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Test it on an inconspicuous area
questions.explanation: Testing reduces the risk of colour loss or fabric damage before treating the visible stain.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe precautions when removing stains from textiles.

questions.prompt: Why should a consumer compare unit prices when choosing between different packet sizes?
options: To judge value for the same quantity
To choose the brightest package
To ignore expiry dates
To increase packaging waste
questions.correctAnswer: To judge value for the same quantity
questions.explanation: Unit price shows the cost per standard amount, making different sizes easier to compare fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use price information to make informed buying decisions.

questions.prompt: Which label information is most useful to a learner who must avoid peanuts?
options: Ingredient list and allergen warning
Package colour only
Advert slogan
Shelf position
questions.correctAnswer: Ingredient list and allergen warning
questions.explanation: Ingredients and allergen statements help consumers avoid foods that may cause allergic reactions.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret label information for safe consumer choices.

questions.prompt: Why should a family distinguish needs from wants when preparing a monthly budget?
options: To prioritise essential spending before optional items
To spend all money on entertainment first
To avoid keeping records
To make prices higher
questions.correctAnswer: To prioritise essential spending before optional items
questions.explanation: Separating needs and wants helps a family protect food, shelter, education, health and savings priorities.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how priorities guide household budgeting decisions.

questions.prompt: Which practice shows work simplification during meal preparation?
options: Arrange tools and ingredients before starting
Walk repeatedly to fetch each item
Use blunt knives deliberately
Cook without a plan or recipe
questions.correctAnswer: Arrange tools and ingredients before starting
questions.explanation: Preparing the workplace reduces wasted movement and saves time and energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply work simplification principles in household tasks.

questions.prompt: Why is good ventilation important in a kitchen using gas or charcoal?
options: It removes heat, odours and combustion fumes
It makes fuel burn without oxygen
It replaces all cleaning
It prevents every burn injury
questions.correctAnswer: It removes heat, odours and combustion fumes
questions.explanation: Ventilation improves comfort and reduces exposure to smoke, steam and harmful gases.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of ventilation in household spaces.

questions.prompt: Which action best reduces household water wastage during laundry?
options: Wash full loads where practical and fix leaking taps
Leave taps running throughout sorting
Rinse one item at a time under continuous flow
Ignore leaks until the bill arrives
questions.correctAnswer: Wash full loads where practical and fix leaking taps
questions.explanation: Efficient loading and leak repair save water without reducing cleanliness.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply conservation practices in household water use.

questions.prompt: Why should household chemicals be stored away from food and children?
options: To prevent poisoning and accidental contamination
To make food cook faster
To improve fabric colour
To avoid reading labels
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent poisoning and accidental contamination
questions.explanation: Chemicals can harm people and contaminate food if stored carelessly or in unlabelled containers.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe storage practices for household chemicals.

questions.prompt: Which response is safest when cooking oil catches fire in a pan?
options: Turn off heat if safe and cover the pan with a metal lid
Pour water onto the burning oil
Carry the pan through the room
Fan the flames with paper
questions.correctAnswer: Turn off heat if safe and cover the pan with a metal lid
questions.explanation: Smothering a grease fire cuts off oxygen; water can spread burning oil and cause severe injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe responses to common kitchen fire hazards.

questions.prompt: Why should waste bins in food preparation areas have covers and be emptied regularly?
options: To reduce pests, odours and contamination
To keep waste warm for longer
To replace handwashing
To make floors slippery
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce pests, odours and contamination
questions.explanation: Covered and regularly emptied bins support hygiene by limiting pest access and microbial spread.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain hygienic disposal of household and kitchen waste.

questions.prompt: Which interior design principle is shown when a room has a clear main point of interest?
options: Emphasis
Rhythm
Proportion
Radiation
questions.correctAnswer: Emphasis
questions.explanation: Emphasis creates a focal point that attracts attention and organises the design.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify how design principles guide room arrangement.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports fair sharing of household duties in a family?
options: Prepare a duty roster based on time, ability and age
Give all tasks to one person permanently
Assign only income earners to rest
Ignore care work because it is unpaid
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare a duty roster based on time, ability and age
questions.explanation: A fair roster considers capacity and availability while recognising the value of household work.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ways of promoting cooperation in family roles.

questions.prompt: A learner plans lunch for a pregnant adolescent using beans, rice, sukuma wiki and oranges. Which nutrition reason makes the menu stronger?
options: It combines energy, plant protein, iron, folate and vitamin C
It removes all need for safe water
It avoids every mineral except sodium
It provides only fat-soluble vitamins
questions.correctAnswer: It combines energy, plant protein, iron, folate and vitamin C
questions.explanation: Pregnancy increases needs for energy, protein, iron and folate, and vitamin C improves plant iron absorption.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan meals that respond to specific life-stage nutrition needs.

questions.prompt: A family member has high blood pressure and wants a healthier daily diet. Which meal-planning adjustment is most suitable?
options: Use less salt and include more vegetables, fruits and unsalted legumes
Add extra salt to every cooked dish
Replace vegetables with sweet drinks
Use processed meats as the main food daily
questions.correctAnswer: Use less salt and include more vegetables, fruits and unsalted legumes
questions.explanation: Reducing sodium and increasing nutrient-dense foods supports healthier eating without giving risky treatment advice.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply healthy eating principles for common diet-related concerns.

questions.prompt: A school canteen serves tea, mandazi and soda as a regular lunch. Which weakness should a Home Science learner identify?
options: The meal is high in refined energy and lacks enough protein and protective foods
The meal contains too many vegetables
The meal has excessive dietary fibre
The meal includes too much clean water
questions.correctAnswer: The meal is high in refined energy and lacks enough protein and protective foods
questions.explanation: A regular lunch should include body-building and protective foods, not mostly refined sugars and fats.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate meals for balance, variety and nutrient adequacy.

questions.prompt: A family wants to reduce food waste after supper. Which practice is most appropriate?
options: Cool leftovers quickly, store them covered and reheat thoroughly before eating
Leave leftovers uncovered overnight for convenience
Mix leftovers with raw meat before storage
Reheat once lightly and keep repeating for several days
questions.correctAnswer: Cool leftovers quickly, store them covered and reheat thoroughly before eating
questions.explanation: Safe leftover handling reduces contamination and spoilage while making good use of food.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe handling practices for cooked food and leftovers.

questions.prompt: A recipe makes 12 scones using 600 g flour. How much flour is needed to make 18 scones of the same size?
questions.explanation: Eighteen is one and a half times twelve, so the flour needed is 600 g multiplied by 1.5.
questions.learningOutcome: Scale recipes accurately for required yield and portion size.

questions.prompt: A cake has a peaked top and coarse texture. Which cause is most likely?
options: Oven temperature was too high
The pan was lined neatly
Ingredients were measured accurately
The cake cooled on a rack
questions.correctAnswer: Oven temperature was too high
questions.explanation: Excess heat can set the outside too quickly, causing a peaked top and rough crumb.
questions.learningOutcome: Diagnose common faults in baked products and suggest causes.

questions.prompt: A sauce made with flour tastes raw and has lumps. Which improvement should be made next time?
options: Cook the roux adequately and add liquid gradually while stirring
Add more raw flour at the end
Stop stirring once liquid is added
Use dirty utensils to increase flavour
questions.correctAnswer: Cook the roux adequately and add liquid gradually while stirring
questions.explanation: Cooking the flour and adding liquid gradually helps develop flavour and prevents lump formation.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply principles of starch cookery in sauce preparation.

questions.prompt: A food product costs KES 1,800 to make 60 portions. If each portion sells for KES 45, what gross profit is made?
options: KES 900
KES 600
questions.correctAnswer: KES 900
questions.explanation: Sales are 60 multiplied by 45, which is KES 2,700. Subtracting KES 1,800 leaves KES 900.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate simple production cost, sales revenue and profit.

questions.prompt: A preserved jam fails to set. Which factor should be checked first?
options: Balance of fruit pectin, acid, sugar and boiling point
Colour of the serving spoon
Shape of the kitchen table
Number of labels printed
questions.correctAnswer: Balance of fruit pectin, acid, sugar and boiling point
questions.explanation: Jam setting depends on enough pectin, acid, sugar concentration and correct boiling.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors affecting quality in sugar-preserved products.

questions.prompt: A dried vegetable product becomes mouldy in storage. Which cause is most likely?
options: It was packed before drying was adequate or stored in damp conditions
It was labelled with the date
It was kept away from pests
It was handled with clean utensils
questions.correctAnswer: It was packed before drying was adequate or stored in damp conditions
questions.explanation: Excess moisture allows mould growth even after drying has started.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify causes of quality loss in dried foods.

questions.prompt: A learner selects fabric for reusable sanitary storage pouches. Which qualities are most important?
options: Washable, durable, colourfast and tightly woven
Transparent, weak and easily torn
Highly flammable and rough
Difficult to clean and loosely constructed
questions.correctAnswer: Washable, durable, colourfast and tightly woven
questions.explanation: A functional pouch should withstand washing, protect contents and remain hygienic during repeated use.
questions.learningOutcome: Select fabrics based on function, care, hygiene and durability.

questions.prompt: A cotton shirt loses colour quickly during washing. Which fabric property is being tested by this problem?
options: Colour fastness
Elastic recovery
Thermal insulation
Absorbency only
questions.correctAnswer: Colour fastness
questions.explanation: Colour fastness is the ability of a dyed fabric to resist fading or bleeding during use and care.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate textile tests to fabric performance during use.

questions.prompt: A learner alters a skirt pattern by adding width evenly at the side seams. Which issue is the learner mainly addressing?
options: Fit around body measurements
Colour harmony
Food safety
Laundry detergent strength
questions.correctAnswer: Fit around body measurements
questions.explanation: Pattern alteration changes dimensions so the garment fits the wearer's body measurements.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply simple pattern alterations to improve garment fit.

questions.prompt: A blouse seam puckers after stitching. Which combination should be checked?
options: Needle size, thread tension, stitch length and fabric handling
Food seasoning, label design and room colour
Shopping receipt, tax record and menu card
Window size, wall texture and flooring
questions.correctAnswer: Needle size, thread tension, stitch length and fabric handling
questions.explanation: Puckering is commonly linked to unsuitable needle, tension, stitch length or feeding of the fabric.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse causes of common seam defects in garment construction.

questions.prompt: A wool sweater stretched after being hung wet on a line. Which care method would have reduced this damage?
options: Dry it flat in shade after gently reshaping
Wring it tightly and hang by the shoulders
Use strong bleach before drying
Iron while dripping wet
questions.correctAnswer: Dry it flat in shade after gently reshaping
questions.explanation: Wet wool can stretch under its own weight, so flat drying helps preserve shape.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply suitable care methods for delicate textile articles.

questions.prompt: A consumer buys a blender with a written warranty. Which action protects the consumer's claim if the blender fails within the warranty period?
options: Keep the receipt and follow the warranty conditions
Throw away all documents immediately
Open and repair the motor without checking terms
Use the blender for tasks warned against in the manual
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the receipt and follow the warranty conditions
questions.explanation: Receipts and warranty terms show purchase details and conditions for repair, replacement or refund.
questions.learningOutcome: Use consumer documents to support responsible redress.

questions.prompt: A shop advertises a large discount but raises the original price first. Which consumer issue is shown?
options: Misleading pricing
Safe storage
Fair measurement
Nutrient conservation
questions.correctAnswer: Misleading pricing
questions.explanation: Inflating the original price can deceive consumers about the real value of a discount.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify misleading practices in advertising and sales promotions.

questions.prompt: A family has KES 4,000 for food, transport and school materials this week. Which budgeting step should happen first?
options: List essential needs and available money before allocating amounts
Buy snacks first and plan with the balance
Ignore prices until after shopping
Spend equally on every item without priority
questions.correctAnswer: List essential needs and available money before allocating amounts
questions.explanation: Budgeting starts by comparing needs with resources so essential items are prioritised.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare simple household budgets based on priorities and resources.

questions.prompt: A household wants to improve a small bedsitter used for cooking, study and sleeping. Which principle should guide arrangement?
options: Zone activities while keeping safe circulation and ventilation
Put the cooker beside bedding to save space
Block the only window for privacy
Store books on the hot cooking surface
questions.correctAnswer: Zone activities while keeping safe circulation and ventilation
questions.explanation: Zoning separates activities and protects safety, comfort and function in limited space.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply space-planning principles to multi-purpose rooms.

questions.prompt: A living room feels crowded because furniture blocks the doorway and windows. Which improvement is most functional?
options: Rearrange furniture to clear circulation paths and allow light and air
Add more large furniture to fill gaps
Close curtains permanently
Place storage in front of the doorway
questions.correctAnswer: Rearrange furniture to clear circulation paths and allow light and air
questions.explanation: Good room planning supports movement, ventilation, daylight and safe use of space.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate room layouts for safety, comfort and function.

questions.prompt: A household cleaning timetable leaves toilet cleaning and food-surface cleaning until the end of the week. What is the main weakness?
options: Hygiene-critical tasks are not scheduled frequently enough
Decorative tasks are too frequent
The timetable has too many people
It includes cleaning materials
questions.correctAnswer: Hygiene-critical tasks are not scheduled frequently enough
questions.explanation: High-risk hygiene areas need regular attention to reduce contamination and disease spread.
questions.learningOutcome: Prioritise household tasks according to health risk and frequency.

questions.prompt: Which household waste plan best supports environmental hygiene?
options: Separate organic waste, recyclables and hazardous waste for suitable disposal
Mix batteries, food scraps and broken glass in one open bag
Burn plastics inside the kitchen
Leave waste uncovered near food storage
questions.correctAnswer: Separate organic waste, recyclables and hazardous waste for suitable disposal
questions.explanation: Separation improves safety and makes composting, recycling and responsible disposal easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply waste-management practices that protect household and community health.

questions.prompt: A caregiver is planning meals for a young child and an elderly adult. Which principle applies to both?
options: Choose nutrient-dense foods with suitable texture and safe hygiene
Serve very hard dry foods only
Ignore fluid needs
Use one large adult portion for everyone
questions.correctAnswer: Choose nutrient-dense foods with suitable texture and safe hygiene
questions.explanation: Vulnerable family members need safe, nutritious food in forms they can chew, swallow and digest comfortably.
questions.learningOutcome: Adapt care practices to different ages and abilities in the family.

questions.prompt: A child drinks an unknown household cleaner. Which response is safest?
options: Call emergency services or a poison centre and follow professional instructions
Force vomiting in every case
Give paraffin to neutralise it
Wait silently until symptoms become severe
questions.correctAnswer: Call emergency services or a poison centre and follow professional instructions
questions.explanation: Chemical ingestion can be dangerous, and some home actions can worsen injury, so urgent expert guidance is needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe emergency responses to household poisoning incidents.

questions.prompt: A learner gets a minor burn from steam during a practical. Which first-aid action is most suitable immediately?
options: Cool the burn under clean running water and remove tight items nearby
Apply cooking oil and wrap tightly
Break any blister to release heat
Rub flour into the burn
questions.correctAnswer: Cool the burn under clean running water and remove tight items nearby
questions.explanation: Cooling reduces heat damage, and removing tight items nearby helps prevent pressure if swelling develops.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe first-aid responses for minor kitchen burns.

questions.prompt: A school Home Science practical room stores knives loosely in a drawer. Which safety improvement is most appropriate?
options: Store knives in a labelled rack or sheath with blades protected
Keep knives under loose papers
Store knives in a bucket of water
Pass knives by throwing them across the bench
questions.correctAnswer: Store knives in a labelled rack or sheath with blades protected
questions.explanation: Protected, organised storage reduces cuts and makes equipment checks easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe organisation of tools and equipment in practical work areas.

questions.prompt: A home-based baker receives feedback that cakes vary in size and price each week. Which record would help most?
options: A standard recipe with yield, ingredient cost and selling price
A list of favourite cake colours only
A blank notebook without dates
A poster of baking tools
questions.correctAnswer: A standard recipe with yield, ingredient cost and selling price
questions.explanation: Production and costing records help maintain consistent portions, quality and pricing.
questions.learningOutcome: Use records to improve consistency in small Home Science enterprises.

questions.prompt: A tailoring group sells aprons but customers complain that straps come loose. Which quality-control check is most relevant?
options: Strength and reinforcement of attachment points
Colour of the sales table
Number of posters used
Taste of packed snacks
questions.correctAnswer: Strength and reinforcement of attachment points
questions.explanation: Functional textile products must have secure seams and attachments at points that receive stress.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate quality features of textile products for customer satisfaction.

questions.prompt: A group wants to sell fruit juice at a school event. Which hygiene control is most important before sales start?
options: Use safe water, clean equipment, covered containers and chilled storage where needed
Prepare juice early and leave it open in the sun
Allow many people to taste from one cup
Use unwashed bottles because they look clean
questions.correctAnswer: Use safe water, clean equipment, covered containers and chilled storage where needed
questions.explanation: Juice can be contaminated easily, so clean water, equipment, covering and temperature control are critical.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply hygiene controls in small-scale food service.

questions.prompt: A family is choosing between charcoal, LPG and electricity for cooking. Which factor set should guide the decision?
options: Cost, availability, safety, ventilation and environmental impact
Only the colour of the stove
Whether neighbours use it
The size of the cooking spoon
questions.correctAnswer: Cost, availability, safety, ventilation and environmental impact
questions.explanation: Fuel choice affects household budget, safety, indoor air quality and sustainability.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare household fuels using practical and safety criteria.

questions.prompt: A nutrition survey finds many learners skip breakfast, buy sugary snacks and feel tired in afternoon lessons. Which conclusion is most reasonable?
options: Poor meal timing and snack choices may be affecting energy and concentration
Skipping breakfast always improves learning
Sugary snacks provide complete nutrition
Water intake has no effect on school performance
questions.correctAnswer: Poor meal timing and snack choices may be affecting energy and concentration
questions.explanation: Regular balanced meals and healthier snacks support energy, concentration and overall wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse eating patterns and propose healthier nutrition practices.

questions.prompt: A household wants to manage a tight food budget without reducing nutrition. Which approach is strongest?
options: Plan menus around legumes, whole grains, seasonal vegetables and safe leftovers
Buy expensive convenience foods daily
Remove all protein foods from meals
Shop without a list to allow impulse choices
questions.correctAnswer: Plan menus around legumes, whole grains, seasonal vegetables and safe leftovers
questions.explanation: Affordable local foods, planning and safe leftover use can protect nutrition while controlling cost.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse food choices for nutrition, cost and household resources.

questions.prompt: A nutrition club wants to reduce anaemia risk among adolescents. Which plan is most complete?
options: Promote iron-rich foods, vitamin C pairings and referral for health concerns
Tell learners to eat sugar only
Ban all beans from school meals
Focus only on packaging of snacks
questions.correctAnswer: Promote iron-rich foods, vitamin C pairings and referral for health concerns
questions.explanation: Food choices can support iron intake and absorption, while persistent symptoms require appropriate health support.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate nutrition interventions for adolescent health concerns.

questions.prompt: A new dried mango product tastes good but becomes sticky inside the package. Which product-development issue should be reviewed?
options: Final moisture level and moisture-proof packaging
Poster font size only
Colour of the sales apron
Number of chairs at the stall
questions.correctAnswer: Final moisture level and moisture-proof packaging
questions.explanation: Dried fruit quality depends on adequate drying and packaging that limits moisture absorption.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse quality faults in preserved food products and suggest improvements.

questions.prompt: A learner compares boiling, steaming and stir-frying vegetables for a practical report. Which conclusion is most accurate?
options: Steaming and quick stir-frying usually conserve more water-soluble nutrients than long boiling
Long boiling always conserves the most vitamin C
All methods have exactly the same nutrient effect
Adding excess water increases every vitamin
questions.correctAnswer: Steaming and quick stir-frying usually conserve more water-soluble nutrients than long boiling
questions.explanation: Short cooking and little water reduce losses of heat-sensitive and water-soluble nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate cooking methods for nutrition, texture and safety.

questions.prompt: A small food business has repeated customer complaints about sour smell in packed mandazi. Which investigation should come first?
options: Check ingredient freshness, frying, cooling, handling and packaging conditions
Change the label colour only
Increase selling price without checking quality
Ignore complaints until sales stop
questions.correctAnswer: Check ingredient freshness, frying, cooling, handling and packaging conditions
questions.explanation: Off odours can arise from poor raw materials, oil quality, moisture, contamination or storage conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse customer feedback to improve food product safety and quality.

questions.prompt: A uniform fabric is attractive but pills badly after a few washes. Which decision is most defensible for a school buyer?
options: Reject it unless testing shows acceptable durability for repeated wear
Choose it because appearance on day one is enough
Ignore care requirements completely
Select it only because it is the brightest colour
questions.correctAnswer: Reject it unless testing shows acceptable durability for repeated wear
questions.explanation: School uniforms need durability, manageable care and long-term appearance, not just initial attractiveness.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate textile products against functional performance criteria.

questions.prompt: A garment pattern is cut off grain to save fabric. Which result is most likely?
options: The garment may twist, hang poorly or lose shape
The garment will become waterproof
All seams will sew themselves straight
The fabric will gain colour fastness
questions.correctAnswer: The garment may twist, hang poorly or lose shape
questions.explanation: Incorrect grain placement affects drape, balance and shape retention in the finished garment.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse effects of pattern layout decisions on garment quality.

questions.prompt: A learner chooses decorative beads for a toddler's dress. Which design decision is safest?
options: Avoid small detachable beads and use secure, washable decoration
Use loose beads on strings near the neckline
Attach sharp pins as decoration
Choose decorations that fall off during washing
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid small detachable beads and use secure, washable decoration
questions.explanation: Children's clothing should avoid choking hazards and use decorations that remain secure and easy to care for.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate garment design choices for safety, comfort and care needs.

questions.prompt: A laundry worker uses strong chlorine bleach on a coloured cotton kanga without testing. Which risk is most likely?
options: Colour loss and fabric damage
Improved colour depth
Permanent stain resistance
Increased fibre strength in every case
questions.correctAnswer: Colour loss and fabric damage
questions.explanation: Strong bleach can remove dye and weaken fibres, especially when used without testing or label guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse risks of unsuitable laundry agents and methods.

questions.prompt: An online seller offers a very cheap pressure cooker but gives no warranty, no physical address and asks for full payment to a personal account. What should a wise consumer do?
options: Verify the seller and terms before paying or choose a more reliable source
Pay quickly because cheap offers are always safe
Ignore warranty information completely
Share personal passwords to speed delivery
questions.correctAnswer: Verify the seller and terms before paying or choose a more reliable source
questions.explanation: Online purchases require checking seller credibility, payment security, warranty and return terms.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate risks and safeguards in online consumer transactions.

questions.prompt: A supermarket promotion offers bulk flour at a lower price per kilogram. Which factor could still make the purchase unwise?
options: The household cannot use or store it safely before quality declines
The unit price is visible
The package has a clear weight
The buyer compares prices
questions.correctAnswer: The household cannot use or store it safely before quality declines
questions.explanation: Bulk buying is economical only when need, storage, quality and cash flow are considered together.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse sales promotions for value, need and storage suitability.

questions.prompt: A family keeps replacing cheap plastic food containers that crack after short use. Which consumer principle is most relevant?
options: Consider life-cycle cost, safety and durability rather than purchase price alone
Always buy the cheapest item first
Ignore material safety for food contact
Choose only by container colour
questions.correctAnswer: Consider life-cycle cost, safety and durability rather than purchase price alone
questions.explanation: A low initial price may cost more over time if the product fails quickly or is unsuitable for food use.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate products using cost, quality, safety and durability criteria.

questions.prompt: A house has damp walls, poor airflow and clothes drying indoors daily. Which solution addresses the root cause best?
options: Improve ventilation, reduce indoor moisture and repair leaks
Paint over stains only
Move furniture tightly against damp walls
Close all windows permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Improve ventilation, reduce indoor moisture and repair leaks
questions.explanation: Dampness control requires reducing moisture sources and increasing airflow, not just covering visible marks.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse household conditions that affect health and comfort.

questions.prompt: A bathroom is shared by young children and an elderly relative. Which design choice best supports safety for different users?
options: Non-slip floor, grab rail, good lighting and reachable storage
Loose mats on a shiny floor
Dark lighting for privacy
Store soap and towels on a very high shelf
questions.correctAnswer: Non-slip floor, grab rail, good lighting and reachable storage
questions.explanation: Universal design reduces falls and supports independent use by people of different ages and abilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate household spaces for accessibility and safety.

questions.prompt: A family's duty roster gives all unpaid household work to one daughter while others rest. Which management weakness is shown?
options: Unfair workload distribution and poor recognition of care work
Excellent delegation and teamwork
Balanced use of human resources
Effective conflict prevention
questions.correctAnswer: Unfair workload distribution and poor recognition of care work
questions.explanation: Fair management recognises unpaid work and shares tasks according to time, ability and responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse family work plans for fairness and cooperation.

questions.prompt: A family using charcoal cooks indoors with closed windows during cold weather. Which risk is most serious?
options: Carbon monoxide and smoke exposure
Improved air quality
Automatic food sterilisation
Increased vitamin content of food
questions.correctAnswer: Carbon monoxide and smoke exposure
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion in poorly ventilated spaces can produce dangerous carbon monoxide and smoke.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse health risks linked to household fuel use and ventilation.

questions.prompt: A Home Science laboratory has food, detergents and sewing tools stored together without labels. Which risk is most urgent?
options: Contamination, poisoning and injury due to poor storage control
Improved speed of practical lessons
Better stock rotation automatically
Lower need for supervision
questions.correctAnswer: Contamination, poisoning and injury due to poor storage control
questions.explanation: Food, chemicals and sharp tools need labelled, separate storage to protect learners and products.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse safety risks in Home Science practical environments.

questions.prompt: A small tailoring enterprise often runs out of thread and delivers late. Which management action addresses the problem best?
options: Keep stock records, plan orders and schedule jobs realistically
Accept every order without checking materials
Stop recording customer deadlines
Cut all fabric before taking measurements
questions.correctAnswer: Keep stock records, plan orders and schedule jobs realistically
questions.explanation: Inventory and scheduling records help meet deadlines without reducing product quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse management practices that support reliable small enterprises.

questions.prompt: A snack producer sells 80 packets at KES 50 each. Ingredients cost KES 2,300, packaging costs KES 600 and transport costs KES 500. What profit is made?
options: KES 600
questions.correctAnswer: KES 600
questions.explanation: Sales total KES 4,000 and costs total KES 3,400, leaving KES 600 profit.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse cost and revenue records to calculate enterprise profit.

questions.prompt: A school is designing a one-week lunch menu for learners with allergies, different faith practices and varied budgets. Which planning approach is strongest?
options: Collect dietary restrictions, use varied affordable foods and label allergens clearly
Serve one dish daily and ignore restrictions
Choose only costly imported foods
Avoid all protein foods to simplify cooking
questions.correctAnswer: Collect dietary restrictions, use varied affordable foods and label allergens clearly
questions.explanation: Inclusive menu planning considers health, culture, cost, variety and clear communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Design meal plans that balance nutrition, cost and diverse dietary needs.

questions.prompt: A community group wants to improve adolescent nutrition using local foods. Which programme design is most complete?
options: Assess needs, teach balanced meals, demonstrate affordable recipes and monitor participation
Distribute sweets only during meetings
Ignore local food availability
Give one lecture without checking outcomes
questions.correctAnswer: Assess needs, teach balanced meals, demonstrate affordable recipes and monitor participation
questions.explanation: A strong programme starts with needs, uses practical local solutions and checks whether participation improves.
questions.learningOutcome: Create nutrition education plans for community wellbeing.

questions.prompt: A learner develops a tomato sauce for sale. Which quality-control plan is most complete?
options: Use sound tomatoes, hygienic processing, suitable acidity, sterilised containers and date labels
Use bruised tomatoes and hide defects with colour
Skip heating to save fuel
Pack in unwashed bottles without labels
questions.correctAnswer: Use sound tomatoes, hygienic processing, suitable acidity, sterilised containers and date labels
questions.explanation: Safe sauce production depends on raw material quality, hygiene, acidity, heat treatment, clean packaging and traceable labels.
questions.learningOutcome: Design safe quality-control steps for preserved food products.

questions.prompt: A learner is developing a low-cost high-protein snack for sale at school. Which development sequence is best?
options: Research need, test recipes, cost portions, check hygiene, package safely and gather feedback
Set the price before knowing ingredients
Copy a product without testing safety
Start selling before preparing any recipe
questions.correctAnswer: Research need, test recipes, cost portions, check hygiene, package safely and gather feedback
questions.explanation: Product development should connect user need, recipe quality, cost, safety, packaging and customer response.
questions.learningOutcome: Create viable Home Science food products using design and enterprise steps.

questions.prompt: A tailoring class wants to reduce fabric waste while making many aprons. Which production plan is most sustainable?
options: Use accurate patterns, economical layout on grain and convert suitable offcuts into small articles
Cut randomly from the middle of each fabric length
Throw all offcuts into mixed waste
Buy extra fabric without measuring requirements
questions.correctAnswer: Use accurate patterns, economical layout on grain and convert suitable offcuts into small articles
questions.explanation: Careful layout protects garment quality, reduces waste and can turn offcuts into useful products.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan garment production that reduces waste and maintains quality.

questions.prompt: A school uniform committee needs to choose fabric for shirts used throughout the year. Which evaluation plan is strongest?
options: Test comfort, strength, colour fastness, shrinkage, care needs, availability and cost
Choose only the brightest colour
Ask one person and skip testing
Ignore laundering because uniforms are new
questions.correctAnswer: Test comfort, strength, colour fastness, shrinkage, care needs, availability and cost
questions.explanation: A uniform fabric must perform well during repeated wear and washing while remaining affordable and available.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop criteria for selecting textiles for specific users and purposes.

questions.prompt: A family wants to reduce monthly utility costs without lowering hygiene or comfort. Which plan is most comprehensive?
options: Fix leaks, use full laundry loads, improve natural lighting, switch off idle appliances and monitor bills
Stop cleaning the home to save water
Leave appliances on for convenience
Use more water because it feels cleaner
questions.correctAnswer: Fix leaks, use full laundry loads, improve natural lighting, switch off idle appliances and monitor bills
questions.explanation: A combined conservation plan saves water and energy while maintaining household health and comfort.
questions.learningOutcome: Design household plans for responsible use of water, energy and money.

questions.prompt: A Home Science room is being prepared for practical lessons involving food, sewing and cleaning agents. Which safety plan is most complete?
options: Clear walkways, labelled storage, hygiene rules, first-aid kit, fire control and emergency contacts
Only decorate walls and ignore equipment checks
Store chemicals in food containers
Keep exits locked during practical lessons
questions.correctAnswer: Clear walkways, labelled storage, hygiene rules, first-aid kit, fire control and emergency contacts
questions.explanation: A practical room needs prevention measures and response resources for food, fire, chemical, tool and injury risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Design safety procedures for Home Science practical environments.

questions.prompt: A family conflict arises because unpaid care work is invisible in budget and time decisions. Which response best supports fair family living?
options: Discuss tasks openly, value care work and agree on a rotating schedule based on capacity
Assign all tasks permanently to one person
Ignore the conflict until resentment grows
Reward only paid work and dismiss home responsibilities
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss tasks openly, value care work and agree on a rotating schedule based on capacity
questions.explanation: Open discussion and fair scheduling recognise household work and support cooperation.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop fair strategies for managing household roles and responsibilities.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to start a reusable shopping-bag enterprise using fabric offcuts. Which business plan element is most important before production begins?
options: Target customers, material supply, costing, quality standard, pricing and marketing channel
Only the learner's favourite fabric colour
A promise to sell without checking demand
A decision to sew without costing materials
questions.correctAnswer: Target customers, material supply, costing, quality standard, pricing and marketing channel
questions.explanation: A viable enterprise links demand, resource supply, cost control, product quality and sales strategy before resources are committed.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a basic plan for a sustainable Home Science enterprise product.
